A passive, healing bird radio you grow yourself · free on Google Play

Grow a tiny ecosystem.
The birds come — and become your radio.

Toris Collection is a free Android app about a small garden that fills with real birds. Plant a few things, then close the app and live your day. Birds find the garden while you're away — and the radio plays their real recorded songs. The ones you have met sing nearer. It can wake you in the morning and fade out as you fall asleep. Nothing to keep up with. You just listen.

How it unfolds

Three small things. The rest becomes your radio.

01 — Plant

Choose a land, plant a little

Kyoto or Charlotte. Plants call insects, and together they call the birds.

02 — Step away

Let time pass

Close the app and live your day. The garden keeps moving without you.

03 — Listen

Your radio grows

The more you meet a bird, the nearer it sings — and the more of them turn up.

What you actually do

Plant. Wait. Meet. Listen.

Six real screens from the app, in the order you'll meet them.

The sound in this clip is the app's own garden radio — field recordings via xeno-canto, used under their Creative Commons licenses, with each recordist credited inside the app.

Morning and night

A radio you wake up to, and fall asleep to.

The birds you have met don't only sing when you open the app.

The cast

The birds of your land, and the ones you have come to know

Every bird you meet is drawn in its own chunky pixel form and kept in your field guide — always there to visit, even after it leaves the garden. Thirty-seven species live in the two lands today.

Quiet promises

The things we will never do to you

We never rush you

No stamina, no timers, no daily duties.

Nothing punishes you

A storm may thin your garden. Your collection never shrinks.

Your radio is always free

Listening is never behind a paywall. Not now, not later.

True to real ecology

Which bird comes, and why, follows a real food web. No invented reasons.

Cuteness, first

The moment a bird arrives, its call, its pixel art. Protected above all.

Made of real things

Real songs, a real web of life

Real recordings

The calls you hear are field recordings from xeno-canto, a community archive of wild bird sound from around the world.

Real relationships

Who eats what, who follows whom — the food web is seeded from GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions), built on real records.

Be there when your radio sings its first bird.
